# Otto — OLT support agent

## Escalation notifications

Both settings are optional because the destination is undecided (`KU-14`).
Unset, the api starts normally, records escalations at
`no_destination_configured`, notifies nobody and logs one
`escalation.no_destination` warning at startup. In the chart,
`api.escalationWebhookSecretName` names a Secret with the keys `url` and,
optionally, `token`. The records live in the `escalations` collection, so a
record and its place in the retry schedule survive a restart. A record whose
process died mid-send is claimed again by the next process after 10 minutes, so
the destination may receive it twice.

# Human access to the support agent's GCP projects

Repository: `re-cinq/Otto`, private. The file that declares who may read a
customer's conversation is `infra/terraform/access/main.tf`; this page explains
it. Cite both at one commit.

**Purpose.** Access control on a system that processes customer conversations.
The api's logs land in Cloud Logging, so whoever can read the project's logs can
read what a customer typed. This page and the terraform root hold work email
addresses, role names and a one-line reason per person, and nothing else.

yet. Until it is, the only member is `user:placeholder@example.com`, and no
real address is committed. Adding the n…

## Why

Escalation is a stated product requirement, not a fallback. Kristian's target and anti-target are both explicit: an insurance robot that took too long to admit it needed to transfer him, versus a tax-authority chat that gave up quickly and was a better experience for it - and the intended destination is a phone call, with OLT contacting the customer as soon as the agent can't answer. Nothing in either meeting says *where* an escalation lands, and OLT has no support platform today. `051` already put a hand-off sentence in the prompt with a guarded placeholder channel, `049` made TMS `unavailable`/`timeout` results branchable specifically for this issue, and `003` lists the hand-off as an unmapped destination. `MongoSessionStore`, so a conversation outlives both its socket and the process,

collection. Every model turn also leaves one row in `auditEntries`, kept 365
days: the session and user ids, when and how long, the model and tool names, the
token counts and how the turn ended, never what anyone wrote. A provider
failover adds a row of its own, with no session or user: the two provider types,
the error code and how long the failed call ran. A tool call that
throws adds one more row and an escalation, so a crashing tool reaches a human

# Support agent chat

## Requirements

### Key Entities

- **connected frame**: carries `sessionId` and `examplePrompts`, and optionally `resumed?: boolean` and `entryCount?: number` (the engine's report of whether the requested session was resumed and how many entries it replays) and `resumeFailure?: 'expired' | 'unknown'`, sent only when the reconnect requested a session id, and as `'expired'` only to the proven owner of the session.

The anti-target is an insurance robot that took too long to admit it needed to transfer him. The target is a tax-authority chat that gave up quickly and was a better experience for it. The client's commitment is to contact the customer as soon as the agent cannot answer, and the intended destination is a phone call.

Neither meeting says _where_ an escalation lands. OLT has no customer support platform, and re:cinq building one was floated and withdrawn in the same breath.
